chapter_theme: Pratyahara (பிரத்தியாகாரம்): drawing the mind inward from the senses, the yogi sees within the one the Vedas searched for; the chapter locates the inner places, below the navel, between the lower openings, where kundalini and the light stand, and defines withdrawal as separating the light from what limits it.
structure_note: Turning inward (578), the locations of the mantra, kundalini and the light (579 to 581, 583, 584), the signs of light and bliss (582), a definition (585), and the fruits (586, 587).

578.reading: If one draws the mind within, looking again and again, one may see many qualities inside, and see here, today, and stay with the one the ancient Veda gladly searched for everywhere.
578.nuance: The contrast is between பண்டு (long ago), எங்கும் (everywhere) and இன்று, இங்கே (today, here): what scripture searched for outside is found within. The one sought is Siva, though not named.

579.reading: They don't know the mantra set twelve finger-breadths below the navel; once they know it, the Lord, called, came and dwelt there.
579.nuance: தாபிக்கும் மந்திரம் (the mantra that is established) is unnamed. The variant நாலிரண்டு (four and two, or eight) changes the measure; the variant குடிபுகுந்தானே (moved in) is close in sense.

580.reading: Two fingers above the root and two fingers below the yoni stands the coiled kundalini, with seven red flames within it; it lies four fingers below the navel.
580.nuance: மூலம் is the base of the spine or the anus, and யோனி the genital place; the seven red flames are not explained and may be the seven centres or seven bodily elements. The two measures of the place do not obviously agree.

581.reading: If you can fix the mind and meditate twelve finger-breadths down from the nose, the great yoga comes to its height and the body never decays.
581.nuance: நாசிக்கு அதோமுகம் may mean below the nose or the downward breath from the nose. மாசித்த is read as மா சித்த (great perfected). The variants யாகுமே and தானே don't change the sense.

582.reading: If a radiant light appears like a line, take it as flawless supreme bliss; if moonlight reaches the throat, the body that recites becomes ecstatic.
582.nuance: The line of light and the moonlight at the throat are signs of practice I can't fix. உன்மத்தம் may be madness, ecstasy or the yogic state unmani; ஓதுவது உன்னுடல் may mean your body, as it recites.

583.reading: Close the lower door firmly, set the mind upon the upper door, keep the spear-like eyes open to the void: this is the way to conquer time.
583.nuance: The lower door is traditionally the anus and the upper the crown of the head. வெளி may be the outer world or the inner void. காலத்தை வெல்லும் may mean conquering death, as in 571.

584.reading: For those who can meditate on the light that gives form, two fingers above the door that lets out excrement and two below the door that lets out the embryo, the light that gives birth stays mingled with them.
584.nuance: The place is the one given in 580 for kundalini, though this verse names only a light. கருவிடும் சோதி may be the light that ends births (கரு விடும், lets the womb go) as well as the light that gives birth; both readings stand.

585.reading: To distinguish at once the bright light from its limiting adjuncts, to dissolve the separation those adjuncts brought, to meditate, to melt and to look within: that is the greatness of pratyahara.
585.nuance: உபாதி (upadhi) is a philosophical term for what limits or conditions the self. The verse defines pratyahara as discrimination and inward looking, not only as drawing in the senses.

586.reading: If one keeps the breath that has gone out from re-entering, becomes skilled and stays firm in certainty, and the mind too is fixed there, the great one will not leave.
586.nuance: புறப்பட்ட வாயுப் புகவிடா is odd as read: it may mean keeping the breath out, or not letting it wander in and out. The last line repeats 575's with பெருந்தகை for புரிசடையோன்.

587.reading: Within one's intention the world appears; with the darkness of aversion gone, one seeks the transcendent one; if one grasps firmly the excellent mind, the vision of knowing makes one equal to the gods.
587.nuance: குறிப்பு is intention, or the fixed point of meditation. விகிர்தன் is a name of Siva as the one beyond change. நங்கி is obscure; I read it as நீங்கி (gone).

links.note: The Kural asks one to draw in the five senses like a tortoise for protection through seven births; Tirumular's withdrawal goes on past restraint to what is found inside: the one the Veda searched for.
Both place the inner power two fingers above the lower opening and two below the genital one: 580 calls it kundalini, 584 only a light.
Both end with the same line, that Siva will not leave, and both make it the fruit of the breath held within.

582 says a line of light is flawless supreme bliss (கோதில் பரானந்தம்) and that the body, with moonlight at the throat, becomes உன்மத்தம். 2779 calls staggering and falling Siva's bliss (திண்டாடி வீழ்கை சிவானந்தம்) and says drinking more brings உன்மத்தம். Both use the word for madness as the sign of bliss, one from the yogi's inner light, the other from the sight of the dance.

587 and 1794 are the same verse with small differences: the world appears within intention (குறிப்பினின் உள்ளே குவலயம் தோன்றும்), the Lord stands when aversion's darkness goes, and the knowing vision makes one like the immortals (அறிப்புறு காட்சி அமரரும் ஆமே). 1794 reads வெறுப்பிருள் நீங்கில் where 587 has the obscure நங்கி, which supports reading 587 as 'gone'. The near-repeat sits once under pratyahara and once under grace.

source_issues: 579: a variant reads நாலிரண்டண்-குலம் for பன்னிரெண் டங்குலம், which changes the measure below the navel.
587: நங்கி is not a known word; it may be a corruption of நீங்கி (gone).
